output.metric: Daily totals exceed the weekly rollup
output.observed_change: For the week of 2026-06-22, summing the daily signup table gives about a third more signups than the weekly rollup reports for the same week.
output.notes: A genuine marketing campaign started mid-window.

blind_spots: marts.signups has no owners recorded in DataHub (ownership lookup returned the entity with no owners) — no team to route MTI-003 to; empty owners is a finding, not a clean result.
marts.signups has no schema fields in DataHub (datahub.schema returned 0 fields) — its day/channel columns and types are not visible from metadata.

Confirmed source-set asymmetry between the two reconciled models: the daily side (marts.signups -> staging.events_daily) draws from BOTH raw.channel_events_raw AND raw.web_sessions, while the weekly side (staging.events_weekly_rollup) draws ONLY from raw.channel_events_raw. The daily sum therefore includes a source the weekly rollup never sees. This is a mapped lineage fact (both UPSTREAM lookups performed), flagged here so the next node does not overlook it.

staging.events_daily is described as bucketing on LOCAL time; the weekly rollup's timezone / week-boundary convention is not recorded, so a 7-day local-time sum may not be comparable to the weekly model's week for 2026-06-22.
raw.web_sessions carries an is_automated flag that not every producer sets — automated/bot visits may be inconsistently included on the daily-only source.

View SQL for the signups, events_daily, and events_weekly_rollup views has NOT been read at the terrain stage; the actual filter/bucket/dedup logic lives in the view text and is unverified — read it before testing how each number is computed.
Every dataset on both branches reports health INCIDENTS: PASS, so no assertion currently covers this daily-vs-weekly reconciliation; green assertions are not evidence the two numbers agree.

Schema-change / metric-definition history was not queried (metric_definition_history and schema_migration_log tables exist but are not exposed by the terrain lookups), so a recent definition change cannot be ruled out from this map.

The symptom window contains a genuine marketing campaign; a real volume lift would raise both models together and does not by itself explain daily exceeding weekly, but campaign timing vs. the local-time day/week boundaries is unverified.

tool_calls.ref: search:signups weekly rollup daily signup table

output.statement: Summing marts.signups over the week of 2026-06-22 exceeds staging.events_weekly_rollup because the daily branch aggregates signup rows from an extra upstream source (raw.web_sessions) that the weekly branch never reads, so the daily sum contains web-session-derived signups the weekly number structurally cannot include — an unreconciled source-set rule mismatch, not a chosen definition.
would_be_confirmed_by: Attributing the daily signup rows for the week of 2026-06-22 by originating source shows web_sessions-derived rows account for approximately the ~1/3 surplus, and excluding them reconciles the daily sum to the weekly rollup.
The events_daily view SQL unions or joins raw.web_sessions as a counted signup source while the events_weekly_rollup view reads only raw.channel_events_raw.
would_be_refuted_by: The events_daily view SQL shows raw.web_sessions is used only for enrichment/filtering (or an inner join that adds no counted rows), so web_sessions contributes zero incremental signup rows to the daily total.
Excluding all web_sessions-attributable rows from the daily sum for the week of 2026-06-22 still leaves the daily total materially (~1/3) above the weekly rollup.
Row-level attribution of the daily table's surplus for that week traces the excess to raw.channel_events_raw (the source shared by both branches) rather than to raw.web_sessions.

output.statement: The definition of a 'signup' was deliberately changed part-way through the window and landed in the daily model (marts.signups / staging.events_daily) but was never propagated to staging.events_weekly_rollup, so from the change date onward — including the week of 2026-06-22 — the daily total counts signups under a newer, broader definition than the weekly rollup measures, producing the ~1/3 excess.
would_be_confirmed_by: metric_definition_history or schema_migration_log records an edit to the signup definition dated within the day-1..day-36 window, on or before the week of 2026-06-22
the daily-minus-weekly excess is ~0 for weeks before that change date and ~1/3 for weeks on/after it — a step change aligned to the edit, not a constant offset
the weekly rollup's view SQL still encodes an older, narrower signup definition (qualifying events/filters) than the daily model's view SQL
would_be_refuted_by: metric_definition_history and schema_migration_log show no change to the signups, events_daily, or events_weekly_rollup definitions anywhere in the window
the ~1/3 daily-over-weekly excess is present in weeks BEFORE any candidate change date at the same magnitude — a constant every-week offset with no step aligned to a definition edit

the daily and weekly view SQL encode the SAME signup definition (identical qualifying events/filters), differing only in source set or time-bucketing — placing the cause in computation/mechanics, not meaning
reconciling both models under a single fixed definition still leaves the ~1/3 gap

output.statement: The ~1/3 by which the daily signup table exceeds the weekly rollup for the week of 2026-06-22 is a real signal, not an artifact: the genuine mid-window marketing campaign drove a surge of distinct, activated, non-bot new customers concentrated on the campaign-active days of that week, and the daily table correctly captures these real people while the weekly rollup simply undercounts them — so the daily number is the trustworthy one.
would_be_confirmed_by: A per-day, per-source breakdown showing the daily excess is concentrated on the specific days the campaign was live, tracking a step-change in signup volume that coincides with the campaign start date.
Cohort/identity checks showing the 'extra' daily signups are distinct new identities with downstream account creation / activation, i.e. real customers.
Prior weeks (no campaign) showing daily and weekly agree, so the gap appears only once the campaign starts.
would_be_refuted_by: The daily 'excess' rows turn out not to be distinct new customers — duplicates, is_automated/bot visits, or identities already counted in the weekly channel data.
A similar ~1/3 daily-over-weekly gap exists in weeks BEFORE the campaign started, showing a standing structural gap rather than campaign-driven behavior.
The excess is flat across the whole week rather than concentrated on campaign-active days, so it does not track real campaign timing.
Downstream activation/account tables show no real accounts corresponding to the extra daily signups.
Recomputing both models from a single common source with one shared week-boundary convention makes them agree, proving the gap is structural/definitional rather than extra real customers.

output.claim: staging.events_daily is defined as an unfiltered COUNT(*) over channel_events_raw only — `SELECT date(occurred_at,'+9 hours') AS bucket_date, channel, COUNT(*) AS events FROM channel_events_raw GROUP BY bucket_date, channel` — applying no signup-qualifying predicate and reading no second source.
output.observation: kind=view; columns bucket_date(TEXT), channel(TEXT), events(TEXT); ddl: CREATE VIEW events_daily AS SELECT date(occurred_at, '+9 hours') AS bucket_date, channel, COUNT(*) AS events FROM channel_events_raw GROUP BY bucket_date, channel

output.claim: staging.events_weekly_rollup is defined as the same unfiltered COUNT(*) over channel_events_raw as events_daily — `SELECT strftime('%Y-W%W', occurred_at) AS bucket_week, channel, COUNT(*) AS events FROM channel_events_raw GROUP BY bucket_week, channel` — encoding the identical signup definition and differing from the daily model ONLY in the time-bucket expression (raw occurred_at week vs. events_daily's occurred_at+9h date), not an older/narrower definition.
output.observation: kind=view; columns bucket_week(TEXT), channel(TEXT), events(TEXT); ddl: CREATE VIEW events_weekly_rollup AS SELECT strftime('%Y-W%W', occurred_at) AS bucket_week, channel, COUNT(*) AS events FROM channel_events_raw GROUP BY bucket_week, channel

output.claim: The marts signups view is a pure rename pass-through of events_daily — `SELECT bucket_date AS day, channel, events AS signups FROM events_daily` — introducing no additional filter, dedup, or definitional change between events_daily and the reported signup metric.
output.observation: kind=view; columns day(TEXT), channel(TEXT), signups(TEXT); ddl: CREATE VIEW signups AS SELECT bucket_date AS day, channel, events AS signups FROM events_daily

output.claim: metric_definition_history contains exactly one row (version 1, day 1, metric 'active_users_daily') and has NO entry referencing signups, events_daily, or events_weekly_rollup anywhere in the day-1..day-36 window, so no recorded signup-definition edit exists to have landed only in the daily model.
output.observation: Single row: {version:1, day:1, metric:'active_users_daily', definition:'distinct customers with at least one non-automated session'}. No row for signups/events_daily/events_weekly_rollup.

output.claim: schema_migration_log contains exactly one row (migration M-0001, day 2, 'CREATE INDEX idx_orders_customer ON orders(customer_code)') — an index on the orders table — and no migration in the window alters the definition of signups, events_daily, or events_weekly_rollup.
output.observation: Single row: {migration_id:'M-0001', day:2, statement:'CREATE INDEX idx_orders_customer ON orders(customer_code)'}. No migration touches the signup models.

output.claim: Across the whole window the daily model total (SUM signups=4437), the weekly model total (SUM events=4437) and the channel_events_raw row count (4437) are all exactly equal, while the week of 2026-06-22 shows daily 1194 vs weekly 895; equal grand totals are inconsistent with the daily model applying a broader signup definition (which would inflate the daily total), so the ~1/3 per-week surplus is a time-bucket boundary artifact that must net to zero across weeks, not a mid-window definition change.

source.query: SELECT (SELECT SUM(CAST(signups AS INTEGER)) FROM signups WHERE day BETWEEN '2026-06-22' AND '2026-06-28') AS daily_sum_wk_0622, (SELECT SUM(CAST(events AS INTEGER)) FROM events_weekly_rollup WHERE bucket_week = strftime('%Y-W%W','2026-06-22')) AS weekly_cnt_wk_0622, (SELECT SUM(CAST(signups AS INTEGER)) FROM signups) AS total_daily_all, (SELECT SUM(CAST(events AS INTEGER)) FROM events_weekly_rollup) AS total_weekly_all, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM channel_events_raw) AS raw_row_count

output.claim: The events_daily view (aliased row-for-row by marts.signups) counts rows from channel_events_raw ONLY and buckets them by local calendar day via date(occurred_at,'+9 hours'); it never reads raw.web_sessions.
output.observation: events_daily ddl: SELECT date(occurred_at, '+9 hours') AS bucket_date, channel, COUNT(*) AS events FROM channel_events_raw GROUP BY bucket_date, channel. signups ddl: SELECT bucket_date AS day, channel, events AS signups FROM events_daily. Neither DDL references web_sessions.

output.claim: The events_weekly_rollup view counts rows from the SAME channel_events_raw table with the same COUNT(*) aggregation, differing from the daily model only in its time-bucket expression: it buckets by UTC week strftime('%Y-W%W', occurred_at) with no +9h local shift — so daily and weekly encode the same signup definition, not different ones.
output.observation: events_weekly_rollup ddl: SELECT strftime('%Y-W%W', occurred_at) AS bucket_week, channel, COUNT(*) AS events FROM channel_events_raw GROUP BY bucket_week, channel. Same source table and COUNT(*) as events_daily; only the bucket key differs (UTC week vs local +9h day).

output.claim: Summed over the entire dataset the daily and weekly models return an identical total that equals the raw row count (4437 = 4437 = 4437), so the daily model contains zero rows the weekly model does not and captures no 'extra real customers'; raw.web_sessions (8781 rows) feeds neither model.

source.query: SELECT (SELECT SUM(CAST(signups AS INTEGER)) FROM signups) AS daily_total, (SELECT SUM(CAST(events AS INTEGER)) FROM events_weekly_rollup) AS weekly_total, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM channel_events_raw) AS raw_rows, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM web_sessions) AS web_sessions_rows

output.claim: For 2026-W25 (the %W week beginning Monday 2026-06-22) the daily-local sum is 1194 vs the weekly-UTC sum 895 (+299 ≈ 33%, i.e. 'about a third more'), but the daily-vs-weekly gap swings BOTH directions across weeks (W22 -61, W23 -5, W24 -328, W25 +299, W26 +2, W27 +93) and the +299 W25 surplus is mirrored by the -328 W24 deficit — a standing week-boundary artifact, not a campaign-week-only surge of net-new signups.

source.query: WITH d AS (SELECT strftime('%Y-W%W', occurred_at, '+9 hours') AS wk, COUNT(*) AS daily_local FROM channel_events_raw GROUP BY wk), w AS (SELECT strftime('%Y-W%W', occurred_at) AS wk, COUNT(*) AS weekly_utc FROM channel_events_raw GROUP BY wk) SELECT COALESCE(d.wk,w.wk) AS week, d.daily_local, w.weekly_utc, COALESCE(d.daily_local,0)-COALESCE(w.weekly_utc,0) AS daily_minus_weekly FROM d LEFT JOIN w ON d.wk=w.wk ORDER BY week

output.claim: The +299 local-W25 daily surplus is composed of channel_events_raw rows relocated across the week boundary by the +9h local shift — 394 rows fall in UTC-W24 but local-W25 (and 95 fall in UTC-W25 but local-W26) — i.e. boundary-straddling rows, not net-new distinct identities, so recomputing both models on one shared week convention would make them agree.

source.query: SELECT strftime('%Y-W%W', occurred_at) AS utc_week, strftime('%Y-W%W', occurred_at, '+9 hours') AS local_week, COUNT(*) AS n FROM channel_events_raw WHERE strftime('%Y-W%W', occurred_at) IN ('2026-W24','2026-W25') OR strftime('%Y-W%W', occurred_at, '+9 hours') IN ('2026-W24','2026-W25') GROUP BY utc_week, local_week ORDER BY utc_week, local_week

output.observation: UTC-W23/local-W24 66; UTC-W24/local-W24 729; UTC-W24/local-W25 394; UTC-W25/local-W25 800; UTC-W25/local-W26 95. The 394 UTC-W24 rows reassigned into local-W25 account for the bulk of the +299 daily surplus in the week of 2026-06-22.

output.claim: DataHub upstream lineage for staging.events_daily lists two source datasets: raw.channel_events_raw and raw.web_sessions.
output.observation: total=2 upstreams returned: raw.channel_events_raw (degree 1, postgres, health INCIDENTS:PASS) and raw.web_sessions (degree 1, postgres, health INCIDENTS:PASS). This declared-lineage source asymmetry is the premise that motivated h1.

output.claim: The events_daily view is defined as SELECT date(occurred_at,'+9 hours') AS bucket_date, channel, COUNT(*) FROM channel_events_raw GROUP BY ... — it reads only channel_events_raw and never references web_sessions.
output.observation: ddl: CREATE VIEW events_daily AS SELECT date(occurred_at, '+9 hours') AS bucket_date, channel, COUNT(*) AS events FROM channel_events_raw GROUP BY bucket_date, channel. web_sessions does not appear in the FROM/JOIN clause at all; the only counted source is channel_events_raw. The declared web_sessions upstream (e1) is a phantom lineage edge unused by the actual computation.

output.claim: The events_weekly_rollup view is defined as SELECT strftime('%Y-W%W', occurred_at) AS bucket_week, channel, COUNT(*) FROM channel_events_raw GROUP BY ... — it also reads only channel_events_raw, so both reconciled branches draw from the same single source and differ only in the time bucket (local +9h day vs UTC %Y-W%W week).
output.observation: ddl: CREATE VIEW events_weekly_rollup AS SELECT strftime('%Y-W%W', occurred_at) AS bucket_week, channel, COUNT(*) AS events FROM channel_events_raw GROUP BY bucket_week, channel. Both events_daily (e2) and events_weekly_rollup read the identical single source channel_events_raw; there is no source-set asymmetry in the actual view text — only a timezone/week-boundary bucketing difference.

output.claim: The signups view (marts.signups) is a pass-through of events_daily: SELECT bucket_date AS day, channel, events AS signups FROM events_daily, so the daily signup count terminates at channel_events_raw only and never counts web_sessions rows.
output.observation: ddl: CREATE VIEW signups AS SELECT bucket_date AS day, channel, events AS signups FROM events_daily. signups selects directly from events_daily with no additional source; combined with e2 the entire daily signup lineage is channel_events_raw only, containing zero web-session-derived rows.

output.claim: For week 2026-W25, summing the signups view over local days 2026-06-22..2026-06-28 gives 1194 while events_weekly_rollup reports 895 — the daily side exceeds the weekly side by 299 (~33%, i.e. about a third more).

source.query: SELECT (SELECT SUM(CAST(signups AS INTEGER)) FROM signups WHERE day BETWEEN '2026-06-22' AND '2026-06-28') AS daily_week_sum, (SELECT SUM(CAST(events AS INTEGER)) FROM events_weekly_rollup WHERE bucket_week = strftime('%Y-W%W','2026-06-22')) AS weekly_rollup_value, strftime('%Y-W%W','2026-06-22') AS week_label

output.observation: daily_week_sum=1194, weekly_rollup_value=895, week_label=2026-W25. Both sides of the disagreement observed together: surplus = 1194-895 = 299 = 33.4% of weekly, matching the reported symptom.

output.claim: The 299-row daily surplus for week 2026-W25 traces entirely to the shared source channel_events_raw via the timezone/week-boundary bucketing difference, not to web_sessions: partitioning channel_events_raw by window membership gives 800 rows in both windows, 394 only in the local-day window, and 95 only in the UTC-week window, so daily_only(394) − weekly_only(95) = 299 = the surplus.

source.query: SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM channel_events_raw WHERE date(occurred_at,'+9 hours') BETWEEN '2026-06-22' AND '2026-06-28' AND strftime('%Y-W%W', occurred_at)='2026-W25') AS in_both, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM channel_events_raw WHERE date(occurred_at,'+9 hours') BETWEEN '2026-06-22' AND '2026-06-28' AND strftime('%Y-W%W', occurred_at)<>'2026-W25') AS daily_only, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM channel_events_raw WHERE (date(occurred_at,'+9 hours') < '2026-06-22' OR date(occurred_at,'+9 hours') > '2026-06-28') AND strftime('%Y-W%W', occurred_at)='2026-W25') AS weekly_only, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM channel_events_raw) AS total_raw_rows

output.observation: in_both=800, daily_only=394, weekly_only=95, total_raw_rows=4437. daily total = 800+394 = 1194 (matches signups sum e5); weekly total = 800+95 = 895 (matches rollup e5). The entire surplus (394-95=299) is channel_events_raw rows that fall inside the +9h local-day window but outside the UTC %Y-W%W week (and vice versa) — the row-level attribution of the excess is the shared source's boundary mismatch, with zero contribution from web_sessions. This is exactly h1's would_be_refuted_by clause 'the excess traces to raw.channel_events_raw rather than to raw.web_sessions'.

output.narrative: For the week of 2026-06-22 (2026-W25), summing the daily signups table gives 1194 versus 895 from the weekly rollup — a +299 (~33%) surplus, matching the reported symptom (e5). Both models read the identical single source channel_events_raw with the same unfiltered COUNT(*), differing ONLY in the time-bucket expression: events_daily buckets by local day via date(occurred_at,'+9 hours') while events_weekly_rollup buckets by UTC week via strftime('%Y-W%W', occurred_at) with no shift (e2, e3, e21, e22). Row-level attribution shows the entire 299 surplus is channel_events_raw rows straddling the week boundary: 394 rows fall inside the +9h local-day window but outside the UTC week, and 95 fall the other way, so 394−95=299, with zero contribution from web_sessions (e6, e25). The daily-minus-weekly gap swings both directions across adjacent weeks (W24 −328, W25 +299), and the daily and weekly grand totals are identical and equal the raw row count (4437=4437=4437), so the surplus is a week-boundary artifact that nets to zero across the window, not extra rows (e16, e24). Nobody chose to have the two models disagree on the day/week boundary convention (local +9h vs UTC); it is an unreconciled timezone mismatch in how the number is computed — instrument_failure.

alternatives_rejected.hypothesis: h1 — instrument_failure via an extra upstream source: the daily branch counts web_sessions-derived signups that the weekly branch never reads.
h2 — definition_change: the signup definition was broadened mid-window in the daily model but not propagated to the weekly rollup.
h3 — customer_behavior: the ~1/3 excess is a real campaign-driven surge of distinct new customers that the daily table correctly captures and the weekly rollup undercounts.

steps.action: Redefine the events_weekly_rollup view to bucket weeks on the SAME local (+9h KST) wall clock as events_daily — change the bucket expression from strftime('%Y-W%W', occurred_at) to strftime('%Y-W%W', occurred_at, '+9 hours') — so both models share one timezone / week-boundary convention. Change the weekly side, not the daily side.
steps.rationale: Both views read the identical single source channel_events_raw with the same unfiltered COUNT(*); the only divergence is the bucket key — events_daily shifts +9h (local KST day) while events_weekly_rollup uses raw UTC week (e2,e3,e22). Row-level attribution shows the entire +299 W25 surplus is boundary-straddling channel_events_raw rows, not extra data (e6,e25), and the daily/weekly grand totals are already identical at 4437 (e16). Adding the +9h modifier makes weekly[W] equal the sum of the local days in that week, so a 7-day local sum reconciles to the weekly value with zero data change. The weekly side is chosen because it is the correct-by-intent convention for a KST business AND, per lineage, has zero downstream consumers (see blast_radius), whereas the daily side feeds marts.signup_conversion_daily.

steps.action: Add a reconciliation assertion / dbt test that fails when, for any week, SUM(marts.signups over that local week) != events_weekly_rollup for the same week, plus a grand-total equality check, and register it in DataHub so it appears in health.
steps.rationale: No assertion currently covers the daily-vs-weekly reconciliation: every dataset reported health INCIDENTS:PASS yet the buckets diverged undetected (e5,e16). A per-week equality test converts the previously silent boundary artifact into a caught regression and guards the alignment from step 1 against future drift.

steps.action: Record an owner for marts.signups in DataHub and have that owner confirm the canonical timezone (KST local vs UTC) before the view change is applied; document the chosen convention as a description on both staging views.
steps.rationale: marts.signups has no owners recorded, so there is no team to arbitrate which timezone is authoritative or to route MTI-003 to. Timezone canonicalization is a semantic decision, not just a mechanical edit; recording an owner both unblocks that decision and closes the routing gap. If no owner objects, default to the existing KST (+9h) daily convention, which preserves the customer-facing daily numbers.

output.verification: Grounded in lineage actually read: events_weekly_rollup DOWNSTREAM returned total 0 (no consumers), so the step-1 change affects nothing downstream — blast_radius is empty; the only asset with a downstream dependency is the daily branch (marts.signups DOWNSTREAM = marts.signup_conversion_daily), which this fix deliberately leaves untouched. To confirm the fix: (1) capture the current marts.signups daily rows and the W22–W27 weekly buckets first. (2) After redefining events_weekly_rollup with the +9h local week, re-run the symptom query for 2026-W25 — SUM(signups) for day BETWEEN '2026-06-22' AND '2026-06-28' should now equal events_weekly_rollup for that week (both 1194), closing the +299 gap (e5). (3) Re-run the per-week diff from e24 across W22–W27 and confirm every daily_local minus weekly value is now 0 (the -61/-5/-328/+299/+2/+93 swings collapse). (4) Verify marts.signups daily values are byte-for-byte unchanged (only the weekly view changed), so marts.signup_conversion_daily is unaffected. (5) Confirm grand totals remain 4437=4437 (e16). (6) The step-2 assertion should pass on this run and fail if the convention ever diverges again.
